intro: PLY to STL converts 3D models from PLY to STL on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to print an object captured with a 3D scanner or rebuilt by photogrammetry. STL is the format every slicer reads (PrusaSlicer, Cura, Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer): it only stores triangles, with no units or colours, as text (ASCII) or binary.

PLY is the format of 3D scanners and photogrammetry: it stores the mesh with a colour per vertex or face, and MeshLab, CloudCompare and Blender open it. PLY does not store units and is taken as millimetres, the usual case; if your model was drawn in centimetres, metres or inches, say so and the conversion turns it into the units you want for the STL. You can also apply a scale, for example 0.5 to print the PLY at half size.

STL does not store colours: if the original has them, the result comes out without them and the note says so. If the PLY has several parts, you can keep them separate inside the STL when the format allows it, merge them into one mesh or get one file per part in a ZIP.

The geometry is not simplified or repaired: every triangle of the PLY reaches the STL unchanged, with duplicate vertices merged. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, checked before the file is processed. Files are deleted automatically when they expire.
steps: Upload one or more PLY files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does my PLY come out tiny or huge?
faq.a: Because the target program assumes other units. Set the units of the original and of the STL.
